newsitem.title: USA: US Senate panel approves more food-stamp money.
newsitem.headline: US Senate panel approves more food-stamp money.

text.p: The Senate Agriculture Committee Tuesday approved 16-1 an additional $1.5 billion in food stamp spending over the next five years.
The funds would be spent on job training and to cover hardship exemptions to people aged 18-50 who otherwise might not be eligible for assistance.
Sen. Jesse Helms, a North Carolina Republican, was the only senator to vote against the spending, which was included in the budget resolution approved last week by Congress.

Under the committee plan, $910 million would be spent on job training and $580 million on hardship exemptions. The exemptions would allow states to provide benefits to childless working-age recipients for longer periods than the three months out of every 36 months dictated by the welfare law passed last year.
The House Agriculture Committee was scheduled to meet Wednesday to act on the same proposal. The items would be wrapped into so-called budget reconciliation bills to be written in each chamber.
